text: Olink’s Proximity Extension Assay (PEA) become leading platform high-throughput, high-sensitivity protein quantification clinical cohort studies. core technology — pairs oligonucleotide-labeled antibodies whose DNA strands hybridize extended upon proximal binding — enables multiplexed detection 92 5,400 proteins minimal sample volumes (~1 µL plasma), readout qPCR NGS yielding Normalized Protein eXpression (NPX) values log₂ scale. guide provides practical, end--end roadmap Olink-based biomarker discovery, covering study design, quality control, differential expression, machine learning, multi-protein signature construction, functional interpretation, reporting standards. Every section written specifically Olink practitioner, code examples drawn OlinkViz package bundled datasets.

title: Best Practices for Olink Protein Biomarker Discovery and Validation
text: proximity extension assay (PEA) couples pairs oligonucleotide-labeled antibodies bind adjacent epitopes target protein. antibodies bind, DNA strands hybridize extended DNA polymerase, creating PCR-amplifiable amplicon unique protein. Quantification performed qPCR (Olink Target 96, Target 48) NGS (Olink Explore), yielding NPX values — normalized log₂-transformed relative protein concentrations. Key properties shape downstream analytical strategy: NPX log₂ scale: Differences groups directly interpretable log₂ fold changes. NPX difference +1 equals 2-fold higher concentration; difference −0.58 equals approximately 0.67-fold (two-thirds). One assay = one protein: Unlike discovery proteomics, peptide identification, protein inference, parsimony grouping step. Olink assay maps single, pre-validated protein target. Missing values predominantly MNAR (missing random): proteins fall assay’s limit detection (LOD) true concentration low. specific implications imputation (see Section 3.5). High sensitivity, wide dynamic range: ~10 logs fM µM, intra-assay CVs 5–15% inter-assay CVs 10–25%. Panel-based coverage: Proteins measured pre-defined panels (Inflammation, Immune Response, Cardiometabolic, Neurology, Oncology, broader Explore panels). efficient means pathway enrichment must account panel’s gene-set composition (see Section 7.1).

title: Best Practices for Olink Protein Biomarker Discovery and Validation
text: Sample size: 20–100 per group. Small N risks false negatives; large N without adequate power planning risks identifying statistically significant biologically irrelevant differences. Use prospective power calculations (Section 2.2). Panel selection: Choose broadest panel(s) relevant disease biology. inflammatory autoimmune conditions, combine Olink Target 96 Inflammation + Immune Response (184 proteins). broader discovery hypothesis-free work, use Explore 1536, 3072, HT. Statistical approach: Use liberal threshold — nominal p < 0.05 without correction, relaxed FDR 10–20%. goal sensitivity: include many true candidates possible. Specificity handled later phases. Fold-change filter: Require minimum effect size (e.g., |log₂FC| > 0.5, ~1.4-fold). eliminates proteins statistically detectable biologically trivial differences. Output: ranked candidate list 15–50 proteins.
code: # Phase 1 discovery with OlinkViz library(OlinkViz) library(dplyr)  data("bansal_baseline57")  # Per-protein Wilcoxon: Healthy vs Long COVID long_data <- bansal_baseline57 %>%   filter(`Long_COVID status` %in% c("Healthy", "Long COVID"))  discovery_results <- lapply(unique(long_data$Assay), function(prot) {   sub <- long_data %>% filter(Assay == prot)   test <- wilcox.test(     NPX ~ `Long_COVID status`,     data = sub,     exact = FALSE   )   data.frame(     Assay  = prot,     p.value = test$p.value,     mean_healthy = mean(sub$NPX[sub$`Long_COVID status` == "Healthy"], na.rm = TRUE),     mean_lc      = mean(sub$NPX[sub$`Long_COVID status` == "Long COVID"], na.rm = TRUE)   ) }) %>% bind_rows()  discovery_results$log2FC <- discovery_results$mean_lc - discovery_results$mean_healthy  # Phase 1 filters: nominal p < 0.05, |log2FC| > 0.5 candidates <- discovery_results %>%   filter(p.value < 0.05, abs(log2FC) > 0.5) %>%   arrange(p.value)  plot_volcano(discovery_results, title = "Phase 1: Discovery")

title: Best Practices for Olink Protein Biomarker Discovery and Validation
text: Power calculations Olink studies must account : Multiple testing burden: Target 96 panel (92 proteins), Bonferroni correction requires α = 0.05/92 ≈ 5.4 × 10⁻⁴ per protein. practice, use BH-FDR 5% verification/validation phases. Realistic effect sizes: Clinically meaningful plasma protein differences often modest — 1.2–1.8 fold (log₂FC = 0.26–0.85). Power calculations use effect sizes drawn prior literature, optimistic guesses. Olink CVs: Intra-assay CV 5–15%, inter-assay CV 10–25%. Use upper bound conservative planning. Practical sample-size guidelines Olink Target 96 discovery (80% power, α = 0.05, two-sided two-sample t-test): FDR-controlled analysis across 92 proteins, multiply per-group N ~1.5–2×. Explore 3072, use BH-FDR throughout increase sample sizes proportionally.

what: Imputation Methods (Ordered by Preference for Olink Data)
title: Best Practices for Olink Protein Biomarker Discovery and Validation
text: -shift imputation (recommended): Draw Gaussian centered (LOD − 1.8σ) σ = 0.3 × SD(observed values). preserves left-censored structure data. Minimal value replacement: Replace LOD LOD/√2. Simple, conservative, widely used Olink literature. Quantile regression imputation (imputeLCMD): sophisticated, dataset-adaptive left-censored imputation. KNN imputation: technical (MCAR) missingness — e.g., sample processing error. use values LOD. Never use mean imputation. systematically overestimates low-abundance proteins — proteins likely differ disease states — attenuates fold changes exactly matter .
code: impute_left_censored <- function(npx_values, lod_values) {   below <- which(npx_values < lod_values)   if (length(below) == 0) return(npx_values)    observed <- npx_values[npx_values >= lod_values]   sd_obs <- sd(observed, na.rm = TRUE)    set.seed(42)   imputed_values <- rnorm(     length(below),     mean = lod_values[below] - 1.8 * sd_obs,     sd   = 0.3 * sd_obs   )   npx_values[below] <- imputed_values   npx_values }

title: Best Practices for Olink Protein Biomarker Discovery and Validation

title: Best Practices for Olink Protein Biomarker Discovery and Validation
text: Olink panels contain groups functionally related proteins (e.g., multiple chemokines Inflammation panel). Two practical considerations: Correlation-aware selection: Lasso selects one representative correlated group. Elastic net retains group. Choose based whether want minimal signature (Lasso) redundant, robust one (Elastic Net). Stability analysis: Run feature selection 100 bootstrap resamples; report often protein selected. Proteins selected >50% resamples stable candidates. Panel dominance check: using multiple panels (e.g., Inflammation + Immune Response), verify final signature isn’t dominated one panel — may indicate panel-level batch artifact.
